## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- The icon is now Plaud's own mark, Plaud's arch symbol on a white tile, as in Plaud's own app icon, in place of the family's drawn mark; `opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`, and the README says Plaud is a trademark of PLAUD LLC.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.
- **New Plaud tools.** A tool Plaud adds later follows `access`, so it runs at the default `"all"`. It is not a script method until a plugin release.
- **Signed links.** Tool results never show a signed link. Audio and transcripts reach a file only through `plaud_export`.
- **Unattended exports.** An export folder is outside the project, so an unattended run needs the `external_directory` rule as well as `plaud_export` (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts, and `/plaud-status` marks it untested.
- **Other accounts in Jelly.** Jelly's declaration names another account's reads as patterns (`plaud-*.get_file` and the rest), so they keep their read-only rules in Jelly. In a Jelly that does not yet write a pattern's rules, those tools follow the plugin's namespace and are denied at Read only, reads included.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- **The recordings source.** `plaud.recordings` names the owner the account's last `probe` named, so every listing of an account, with a cursor or without, needs a probe of it since OpenCode started (`UNAVAILABLE` otherwise). A cursor issued for another Plaud user than the one the probe names is refused (`CURSOR_INVALID`). The source contract `v0.1.0` does not let a page read who is signed in itself (source-contract#30).
- **Other accounts through the source contract.** The source contract `v0.1.0` derives a consumer's session rules for `plaud.recordings` as `plaud_get_current_user` and `plaud_list_files`, whatever the account, while another account's reads are its own server's, `plaud-<alias>_…`. So a consumer's fenced read of an account other than `default` is refused by the session until the contract can name a per-account server. Scripts and the model are unaffected.
- **A day's query spans three days.** Plaud's date filter takes whole days (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in a time zone its docs do not name, so the plugin's narrowest query asks for a day and one either side. While Plaud ignores `page` under a date filter, three days that hold more recordings than one page of Plaud's answer keep failing with `PLAUD_READ_FAILED` (the cursor stays put, so nothing is lost) until Plaud honours `page`, or until such a listing is started after those days.
- **Plaud's limits.** Plaud publishes no request limit for its server, and its docs say `list_files` ignores `page` and `page_size` under a date filter, which `events_list` always sets. So when a page that is not empty repeats the one before, whatever its length, the plugin cannot tell whether Plaud sent every recording, and lists the week again one day at a time; when a day's query still repeats, it fails with `PLAUD_READ_FAILED` before the cursor moves, rather than skip a recording ([Plaud MCP](https://docs.plaud.ai/plaud-mcp-cli/mcp), "Filtering recordings with `list_files`"). The source's answers in the conformance test are invented in the shapes those docs give, not recorded from a live account.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.3] - 2026-11-15

### Added

- Plaud's source under the shared source contract, `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.1.0: `package.json`'s
  new top-level `sources` key declares `plaud.recordings`, an `events` source of kind `meeting`, read with
  `events_list` and input `source: "recordings"`, for a named account (`accounts.named`). Its operations are
  `get_current_user` and `list_files`, with `get_current_user` its one identity operation; it is private, free
  (`cost.class: "free"`), and `maxBytes` is 262,144. The tools RPC is `plaud.recordings.tools` and the probe action
  `plaud_probe`. Memory and jelly read the declaration from the installed package, with the contract's `descriptor`.
- For Memory and every consumer: the tools RPC method `probe` (action `plaud_probe`, allowed by the default rules at
  every `access`) answers whose sign-in an account is, `{ source: "recordings", account, owner, trust }`, from that
  account's `get_current_user`, and reads no recording. The owner is `mailto:<email>` when Plaud gives an email, or
  `plaud:<user id>`, with the same label on every page.
- For Memory and every consumer: `events_list` with `source: "recordings"` reads only `list_files`. Its page names the
  owner the account's last `probe` named, which the plugin keeps per account, and carries `plugin` and `refused[]`: a
  recording whose title holds a secret is refused for good with `reason: "secret"`, and the cursor moves past it. Its
  cursor is the contract's version 2, bound to the plugin, the source and the account, and holds the owner's id.
  **Every listing of an account, with a cursor or without, needs a `probe` of that account since OpenCode started**,
  or it answers `UNAVAILABLE` before any read: a page's owner is only ever one a probe read from Plaud, never a
  cursor's, whose binding hash is no signature. A listing with a
  cursor must name its `account` (`INPUT_INVALID`), another account's cursor is `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`, and a cursor from
  another source or plugin, or contract 1's, is `CURSOR_INVALID`: start again with `since`. A cursor whose owner is
  not the one the account's last probe named is `CURSOR_INVALID` too, as after a restart with another Plaud user on the
  account. An account the plugin does not have is
  `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`, and a source it does not have `SOURCE_UNKNOWN`.
- `npm test` runs the contract's conformance kit over the declaration, `events_list` and `probe`
  (`test/conformance.test.ts`), on invented Plaud answers with no Plaud call (`test/fixtures/sources.json`), and writes
  `reports/conformance-report.json` (git-ignored, the same bytes on every run) for a release to attach. Every check
  that applies passes. The report stays incomplete on the kit's expired-cursor check: Plaud keeps every recording until
  the person deletes it, so no history behind a cursor is lost and the plugin never answers `CURSOR_EXPIRED`, which
  v0.1.0 has no way to say.

### Changed

- The tools RPC and the events contract are the source contract's, bundled into `dist/index.js` from the pinned tag:
  `src/host/events-list.ts`, the shared part of `src/host/tools-rpc.ts`, its two shared test suites
  (`test/tools-rpc.test.ts`, `test/resolve.test.ts`, which the package runs verbatim) and their `check-copies` pins are
  deleted. Plaud's part of the RPC is the `ToolsRpcPlugin` value in `src/host/tools-rpc.ts`. The RPC id
  `plaud.recordings.tools`, its methods and their answers are unchanged, and `events_list` without `source`, or with
  `source: "plaud"`, lists exactly as before, with its own cursor, for scripts and Memory's collector; only an unknown
  `source` is now `SOURCE_UNKNOWN` rather than `INPUT_INVALID`.
- `events_list` never loses a recording when `list_files` ignores `page` under a date filter, as Plaud's docs say it

## [0.0.2] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- `test/fixtures/live-tools.json`, Plaud's tool list for a signed-in user, captured live on 14 November 2026, and a test
  that fails when the declaration and that list disagree. The declaration already matches it: 5 served reads plus the
  plugin's own `recent`, `events_list` and `export`.

### Changed

- The `jelly` declaration names another account's reads as patterns: `plaud-*.list_files`, `plaud-*.get_file`,
  `plaud-*.get_note`, `plaud-*.get_transcript` and `plaud-*.get_current_user`, each with the default account's
  permission and `readOnly: true` (13 tools, 12 read-only). Jelly writes their rules at the engine's names, so another
  account's reads run at Read only and in a read-only helper, in a Jelly that writes a pattern tool's rules.
- `docs/jelly.md` says Jelly reads the accounts (the sign-in's `account` option) and the patterns above. The README's
  Known limits say so too.
- `scripts/check-upstream.mjs` says a new upstream tool follows `access`, so it runs at the default `all`.
- `package.json` is `"private": true`, so nothing can be published to npm by accident; installs from the Git tag are
  unaffected. The release workflow also refuses a `package.json` that is not private or not in its canonical form.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.

- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6. A later 2.2 release starts, and `/plaud-status` marks it untested.
- **Other accounts in Jelly.** Jelly's declaration names another account's reads as patterns (`plaud-*.get_file` and the rest), so they keep their read-only rules in Jelly. In a Jelly that does not yet write a pattern's rules, those tools follow the plugin's namespace and are denied at Read only, reads included.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.
